summary: 1. Ore beat plan by 97.4% (3,410 BCM against a 1,727.8 BCM target) on a single-grade MG blend, the first all-MG ore day of the new cycle, but the daily total still missed by 1.5% (21,917 BCM against 22,255.3 BCM) because waste ran 9.8% under plan. 2. 2. The crusher lost about 12h15m to maintenance, the heaviest single-day downtime of the August cycle, and fed only 1,792 BCM, the cycle's lowest daily feed — MTD crusher stockpile throughput sits at 10,863 LCM against the 124,000 LCM monthly plan, 8.8%. 3. 3. MTD production sits at 84,537 BCM against an 89,021.2 BCM target, -5.0% at day 4 of 31, with 27 days remaining in the cycle. 4. 4. Drilling posted its best day of the cycle so far, 2,898 m against a 2,581.2 m target (+12.3%), and the Daily Drill Sampling Record logged 130 samples — a new high for the entire July/August dataset, surpassing the prior July 13 high of 118. 5. DR-343's standing "Faulty Drifter" fault, which had cleared for the first time in the Jul 27 report after 16+ days down, reopens on Jul 28 under a different description ("Faulty compressor oil separator element replaced, Water injection problem rectified") — resolving last pass's open question in the negative. 6. DR-125 logs the identical fault description the same afternoon, and DR-139 separately develops a new "Faulty percussion" fault — three drill-fleet fault entries opening within hours of each other. 7. EX-253's Jul 27 "Swing problem" (previously unspecified) is confirmed Jul 28 as a hard mechanical failure — "Swing Bearing Failure," 41.67% availability, a new fault entry rather than a continuation. 8. Elsewhere in the ancillary fleet, WD-145 (the site's only Wheel Dozer) fully recovers from Jul 27's full-category outage. 9. The Week 31-32 bi-weekly plan deck lands (`Weekly Plan ADW W301_32.pdf`, 28 Jul-10 Aug). EX-123 is written out for a fourth consecutive bi-weekly deck (0% PA, no recovery date); DR-124/125/139 are written out for a fifth straight deck, and the same equipment table lists a duplicate "DR-125" row at 78% PA alongside DR-341/342/343 — a likely copy-paste error. More notably, the deck's weekly production-schedule totals (Week 31: 410,477 t, Week 32: 412,268 t) are byte-identical to the W30-31 deck's own totals for the immediately preceding week pair, and the drill-fleet total row (782 service hrs, 53% PA) also repeats exactly — worth a direct check with JRAR planning on whether these tables are being recalculated per deck or carried forward from a template. No new INX-SUM survey file has landed for Day 4 of the August cycle (which would reconcile Jul 28's truck count); the survey MTD gap still reflects Day 3's -31.76%. This is a dashboard-scoped run (per the 74th/75th pass pattern) — Important References and the Task Feedback Log were not processed.
